messages:
support-ops: FYI AcmeCorp just escalated — after last night's batcher config rollout they see p95 ~600ms -> p95 ~1s and p99 climbing from ~1.2s -> 2.4s, occasional 504s. Customer says failures spike during small prompt bursts. I attached their minimal repro and partial logs below.

sre-bot: ALERT: tenant=acmecorp p99_latency=2400ms over window=5m threshold=1000ms

maria: this was the canary->prod rollout of batcher tuning (PR #4127). Changes: default hold_ms increased from 2 -> 20, batch_size_target bumped 8 -> 32 for better throughput. Rollout completed 2026-03-16T02:03Z.

alex: thx. can someone paste the tenant override / recent config for Acme? need to know if they have tenant-specific grace/hold policy. also send a few trace ids for 504s.

tian: copying customer repro (redacted key):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw/gpt-13b", "input":"short prompt"}'
```
Logs from their tenant network: 
```
[2026-03-16T21:58:02Z] req_id=abc123 queue_wait_ms=27 batch_size=18 exec_ms=210 total_ms=244 status=200
[2026-03-16T21:59:05Z] req_id=def456 queue_wait_ms=580 batch_size=34 exec_ms=180 total_ms=760 status=200
[2026-03-16T22:04:11Z] req_id=ghi789 queue_wait_ms=1830 batch_size=42 exec_ms=220 total_ms=2050 status=504
```
Customer says the big queue_waits line up with small prompt bursts from their mobile app.

alex: that log shows the queue_wait ballooning — likely because hold_ms=20 is letting many tiny requests accumulate to hit larger batch sizes. For tiny tokens, cost-optimize hold allows throughput but hurts tail latency. Hypothesis: the batcher is prioritizing batch size over latency for this tenant.

maria: confirmed tenant config snapshot: `{"batcher":{"hold_ms":20, "max_batch_size":64, "target_batch_size":32, "grace_ms":8}}` (inherited from org-wide profile applied in the rollout).

alex: mitigation options (short-term):
- set tenant override to `hold_ms: 2` (restore latency-first behavior)
- or set `prefer_latency: true` for acme to prioritize small batches
- route Acme to dedicated low-latency pool (if available)

quick command to patch tenant (internal API):
```
PATCH /internal/tenants/acme/config
Content-Type: application/json
{"batcher":{"hold_ms":2}}
```

maria: i'll push a 10% canary change for Acme (will target 10% of their traffic to the new override) so we can verify impact before full rollback. Running: `infractl tenant-patch acme --patch '{"batcher": {"hold_ms":2}}' --canary 10`

support-ops: shared the canary plan with customer and asked them to exercise the failing mobile flow for ~15 minutes.

eng-oncall: added tracing hooks to capture `queue_wait_ms` and `batch_size` per request for this tenant and increased retention for those traces for 1h. Also enabled extra sampling for 504/5xxs.

(10 minutes later)

tian: customer reports p99 down to ~900ms on canaryed requests and 504s stopped for those routed to canary. Full customer test link: https://acme-repro.example.com/session/321

alex: great — that confirms the hold window was the primary driver. Going to roll to 100% but will monitor closely.

maria: rolling to 100% now: `infractl tenant-patch acme --patch '{"batcher": {"hold_ms":2}}' --canary 100`

support-ops: customer confirms overall latency improved, still sees occasional spikes ~1.2s during extreme bursts.

alex: follow-ups:
- create runbook entry: when p99 spikes for small-prompt tenant, check `hold_ms` and `target_batch_size` overrides and prefer_latency flag.
- expose tenant-level `latency_sla` override in console to prevent throughput-oriented rollouts from applying to latency-sensitive tenants.
- add a regression test in the rollout pipeline that simulates tiny-prompt microbursts and measures p99.

tian: created support ticket INF-2045 and logged customer confirmation. Sending internal note to account team to explain the fix.

maria: will add gating to future rollout PRs to require p99 < 1s on a tiny-prompt synthetic before promoting the batch-size increase.

alex: thanks everyone. marking resolved for now; will keep the increased tracing for 2 hours. :thumbsup:
